work_order.understanding:
QA's retest says BUG-2 is fixed and I am not reopening it: the skip link is a 44x44 in-flow target 16-18px clear of the brand link, and T-7 now measures it in its focused state, which last round's instrument could not do. 28 of 29 cases are green. One bug remains, BUG-4, and it is introduced by this PR. QA reproduced it three times with an identical measurement (run8.log line 76: linkWidth 120, spanClient 120, spanScroll 267, headerFreePx 1160, truncated true) and I reproduced it myself to the pixel against this build's own served stylesheet.

**The previous order's diagnosis was right and its fix was wrong, and the second is the more useful thing to say.** v3 correctly found that the display name was unbounded and that the nav could not shrink. Both halves held: BUG-3's 548px overflow is gone and T-9/T-10/T-11 pass. What v3 got wrong was the remedy it reached for. It concluded that the nav needed a fixed `max-w-[120px]` ceiling to bound the name, and then justified the number by comparing it to one string: "120px is above the product's own fixture ('Ada Q Harness' is 118.19px) so ordinary names are not truncated." That is an argument from a single sample, and it is false in general -- 'Bartholomew Featherstonehaugh' needs 267px and is not a fixture, it is a name. More to the point, I measured whether the ceiling was load-bearing at all, and it is not. `min-w-0` on the nav, which v3 also added and which IS load-bearing, is on its own sufficient: I deleted `max-w-[120px]` in the harness and the 80-character unbroken name still produced scrollWidth === clientWidth at every width from 320 to 1920, with zero undersized controls and zero sub-8px pairs. The cap was not preventing the overflow. It was buying a 360px guarantee nobody needed at the price of truncating a name on a screen with 1160px free, which is what v3 wrote down in its own risks section ("a name longer than ~14 characters on a 1280 screen will show an ellipsis") and shipped anyway. That is the loop this stage exists to catch: a fix chosen to satisfy a measured claim, verified against the measurement that was asked for, and never checked against the criterion it was quietly breaking.

**Deleting the cap alone is also not enough, and this is the part worth writing down.** With the cap gone and nothing else changed, the flex row shrinks every item proportionally, so at 360px the sign-out control falls from 82.19px to 50.91px -- its own label is 66.19px, so the control is now narrower than its text. That is a new defect, traded for the old one. The name link has to be the ONLY item that gives ground. `shrink-0` on the Groups link and on the sign-out `<form>` does that, and I verified the placement by measurement rather than by reasoning: on the `<form>` it works, on the `<button>` inside the form it does not, because the form is the flex item and the button is not. With that, every measurement is clean -- 55 rows across 5 names x 11 widths (320, 360, 375, 414, 480, 600, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440, 1920), zero overflow, zero undersized controls, zero sub-8px pairs, sign-out pinned at 82.19px everywhere, and 'Bartholomew Featherstonehaugh' rendering in full at every width from 600 up.

**I am not correcting any criterion.** AC-8 says the name "appears everywhere the user is shown, including the top bar" and AC-14 says it is "shortened with an ellipsis if it does not fit". Those two agree once "if it does not fit" is read for what it says: an ellipsis is owed where there is no room and is a defect where there is. On a 360px screen the 29-character name is genuinely truncated under the fix, and that is correct -- there is no room. On a 1280px screen it is not, and that is BUG-4. v3's cap made the second case behave like the first. The criteria were right; the code was wrong. AC-15 is new and states the room-dependent rule so the next QA run, which gets these criteria and no memory of this one, checks it explicitly rather than inferring it.
work_order.root_cause:
`max-w-[120px]` in src/components/ui/top-bar.tsx line 35 is an unconditional pixel ceiling on the display-name link, so it truncates at every viewport rather than only where the bar is actually tight. It is the sole cause of BUG-4: on a 1280px header the name link is pinned to 120px while the span inside it needs 267px, so 'Bartholomew Featherstonehaugh' renders as 'Bartholome...' with 1160px of the header empty. AC-8 asks that the name appear everywhere the user is shown, including the top bar, and on a desktop browser it does not.

The cap was introduced by v3 as the remedy for BUG-3, and it was never load-bearing. I removed it in a harness built from this build's own served stylesheet and re-measured the exact case it was added for -- the 80-character unbroken name -- at 320, 360, 375, 414, 480, 600, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920: scrollWidth === clientWidth at every width, undersized controls [], pairs within 8px []. The `min-w-0` v3 put on the <nav>, which is the part that IS load-bearing, is sufficient on its own. A flex item's automatic minimum size is its min-content width, and `min-w-0` on the nav is what lets the row shrink below its content; once the nav can shrink, the name link inside it shrinks with it.

The cap's justification was an argument from one sample. v3 wrote "120px is above the product's own fixture ('Ada Q Harness' is 118.19px) so ordinary names are not truncated", which is true of that one string and false of the next one over -- and v3's own risks section recorded the consequence ("a name longer than ~14 characters on a 1280 screen will show an ellipsis") and shipped it anyway.

Deleting the cap alone is not the fix either, and this is the second half of the cause. With the ceiling gone and nothing else changed, flexbox distributes the shrink across every item in the row in proportion to their base sizes, so at 360px the sign-out control falls from 82.19px to 50.91px against a 66.19px label: the control becomes narrower than its own text. The row needs the name to be the only item that gives ground, which means the Groups link and the sign-out <form> need `flex-shrink: 0`. It has to go on the <form>, not on the <button> inside it -- the form is the nav's flex item; I measured both and only the form placement holds the control at 82.19px.
work_order.approach:
Two files, both small, both measured. The change is a deletion plus a pinning, not a new mechanism.

**1. src/components/ui/top-bar.tsx — delete `max-w-[120px]`, add `shrink-0` to two siblings.**

(a) On the display-name link at line 35, delete `max-w-[120px]` from the className, leaving `"inline-flex min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] items-center text-base"`. Keep `min-w-[44px]` exactly as it is: it is a floor, the 44px minimum is on both axes, and T-10's one-character-name case (44x44) depends on it. Keep `<span className="truncate">` and keep `min-w-0` on the nav -- both are load-bearing and neither is what caused BUG-4. `truncate` is what makes the ellipsis render at all when the bar IS tight (text-overflow does not reliably apply to a flex container's own text), and `min-w-0` on the nav is what stops the row refusing to shrink. With the ceiling gone the name takes its content width up to the point where the siblings would be squeezed, and the truncate span takes over from there.

(b) Add `shrink-0` to the Groups link at line 24 and to the `<form>` that wraps the sign-out button. The Groups link's className becomes `"shrink-0 min-h-[44px] leading-[44px] text-base"`. The sign-out form is in src/components/shell.tsx, not top-bar.tsx -- see file 2.

(c) Rewrite the comment above the name link. It currently explains the ceiling ("plus a ceiling: ... the max-width is what bounds this item's min-content contribution, without which the row cannot shrink at all") and that sentence is now false: the max-width is gone and the row shrinks fine without it. The replacement should say what the classes actually do -- the span makes the ellipsis render, the nav's min-w-0 lets the row shrink, and shrink-0 on the siblings is what keeps the shrink coming from the name alone rather than from the sign-out control. Leaving the stale comment in place is how this defect gets reintroduced.

**2. src/components/shell.tsx — `shrink-0` on the sign-out form.** Add `shrink-0` to the `<form action={signOut}>` at line 33. On the `<form>`, NOT on the `<button>`: the form is the nav's flex item and the button is not, so `shrink-0` on the button has no effect on the row at all. I measured both placements -- on the form the sign-out control holds 82.19px at 360 and at 1280; on the button it still collapses to 50.91px. Change nothing else in this file; the button's own classes are correct and QA re-verified it at 44px this round.

**3. tests/components/ui.test.tsx — replace the case that pins the defect.** The existing case at line 291, `'a one-word display name is capped, truncated and shrinkable'`, asserts `expect(nameLink.className).toContain('max-w-[120px]')`. That assertion is the defect, encoded as a test: it fails on the fixed source and passes on the broken one. Rewrite the case to `'a one-word display name is truncated, not capped, and the name is the only item that shrinks'` and assert instead that (i) the name link does NOT match /max-w-\[\d/, which is the reproduction of BUG-4 and the regression guard against any future ceiling returning, (ii) the span inside still carries `truncate`, (iii) the nav still carries `min-w-0`, and (iv) the Groups link and the sign-out form both carry `shrink-0`. Note that (iv) needs a Shell render, not a TopBar render, because the form lives in shell.tsx -- `<Shell user={...}>` renders TopBar plus the SignOutControl, so one render covers all five assertions. Keep the existing comment above the describe block about jsdom computing no layout; it is still correct and still load-bearing.

**Measured before proposing, not after.** Every number above comes from a harness built out of this build's own `served.css` (the stylesheet QA captured at 71e2e89 and md5-verified against the served preview), driving headless Chromium at 11 viewport widths. Shipped baseline, reproducing QA: at 1280 the ordinary name measures linkWidth 120, spanClient 120, spanScroll 267, headerFree 1160, truncated true -- QA's log line 76 to the digit. After the fix: 'Bartholomew Featherstonehaugh' renders in full (266.98px, not truncated) at 1280 and at every width from 600 up; scrollWidth === clientWidth at all 11 widths for all 5 names including the 80-character unbroken word; undersized controls [] and sub-8px pairs [] on all 55 rows; sign-out pinned at 82.19px and Groups at 57.05px everywhere. The one case that still truncates the ordinary name is 320-480px, where there is genuinely no room -- that is AC-14's "shortened with an ellipsis if it does not fit", not a defect, and AC-15 says so explicitly so the next run does not file it.

Deliberately NOT done: no criterion is rewritten (AC-8 and AC-14 are both correct and AC-14 is satisfied by this fix); no change to docs/ui.md; no change to the brand link, the header's own classes, the skip link or globals.css, all of which QA re-verified this round; no change to the schema's 80-character name cap, which is what makes the worst case legal rather than impossible; and no build-time guard against a fixed pixel ceiling reappearing in a flex row -- that is the same class of later ticket as the theme-namespace guard v3 deferred.

alternatives_considered.approach: Replace max-w-[120px] with a viewport-relative ceiling such as max-w-[45%].
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It keeps the mechanism that caused BUG-4 — a ceiling that applies at every viewport — and just makes the ceiling track the viewport. It happens to be harmless at 1280 because the name is under 45% of the header, but it is a magic fraction with no stated basis, it silently changes with the viewport rather than with the content, and it would re-truncate at exactly the widths where a long name and a narrow bar meet. I measured it (the capFrac variant) and it works, which is the problem: it works by being large enough not to matter, which is the same non-argument v3 made with 120px.

alternatives_considered.approach: Raise the ceiling to a value above every name the schema accepts — max-w-[600px] or similar.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It cannot be done: the schema accepts 80 unbroken characters, which measure 1028px at 1280. Any ceiling that does not bind is not a ceiling, and any ceiling that does bind reintroduces BUG-4 at a different width. This is the shape of v3's mistake and it is not a fix, it is a bigger version of the same mistake.

alternatives_considered.approach: Shorten the display name in the database or at render time — CSS text-overflow on a single line with no truncation limit, or JS ellipsis at a character count.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The CSS half already exists and is correct (the truncate span). The JS half would put a second, divergent truncation rule in the codebase that jsdom can test and the browser cannot, which is the inverse of this codebase's stated position — and it would still truncate at 1280, which is the defect.

alternatives_considered.approach: Let the top bar wrap to two lines at narrow widths so the name is always shown in full.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is a real answer to the underlying tension and it is a larger product change than this ticket should make: it alters the header's height at every width, which puts the 44px sweep (AC-12) and the 8px separation rule in play against a control nobody has measured in a two-line bar, and docs/ui.md describes a single top bar. v3 named this same alternative and deferred it for the same reason. It remains the right answer if a maintainer decides the name is never allowed to be shortened, and it should be a separate ticket with its own measurements, not smuggled into a bug fix.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave the ceiling and instead widen the header or reduce the name's font size at wide viewports.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Treats the symptom. The header is not narrow at 1280 — it has 1160px free. No amount of extra room makes a fixed 120px ceiling stop truncating, because the ceiling is applied before the available space is ever consulted.

review.title: rounded-radius emits no CSS rule at all, so every rounded surface in the product renders with square corners. This is the identical bug shape commit d365f2c fixed for the spacing tokens — a Tailwind v4 utility name that does not match any declared @theme namespace, which compiles to nothing silently — and it survived that fix and all 86 tests because the token was named --radius and the utility reads rounded-radius.

rounded-radius emits no CSS rule at all, so every rounded surface in the product renders with square corners. This is the identical bug shape commit d365f2c fixed for the spacing tokens — a Tailwind v4 utility name that does not match any declared @theme namespace, which compiles to nothing silently — and it survived that fix and all 86 tests because the token was named --radius and the utility reads rounded-radius.

`src/components/ui/button.tsx:48`

Evidence: globals.css:33 declares `--radius: 8px`. In Tailwind v4 that namespace emits `.rounded{border-radius:var(--radius)}`, which is present in the built stylesheet (.next/static/chunks/3u8v4v7dsedzb.css); grep -c 'rounded-radius' on that file returns 0, and the only rounded utility it emits is `.rounded{border-radius:var(--radius)}`. Measured in Chromium against the running production build on /sign-in: getComputedStyle submit button borderRadius = '0px', .card = '0px', both visible inputs (326x44) = '0px'. Isolated A/B on the same stylesheet: an element with class `rounded-radius` computes to 0px and one with `rounded` computes to 8px. The class name survives into the JS chunks (it is a string in the component), so grepping the bundle finds it and reading the component looks correct — only the stylesheet shows the gap. Six call sites across five files: button.tsx:48 and :82, card.tsx:9, skeleton.tsx:6, input.tsx:34, dialog.tsx:76. docs/ui.md:27 specifies `--radius` 8px for 'Cards, inputs, buttons. One radius for the product', so this is the designed token not reaching the screen. No test asserts a radius, and 86 pass with lint and tsc clean. Introduced in 17bd4eee.

Fix: Rename the six `rounded-radius` occurrences to `rounded`, which is the utility `--radius: 8px` actually generates. Do not rename the token to `--radius-radius` to keep the class name — one radius for the product is what docs/ui.md:27 asks for, and `rounded` is the shorter spelling of the same thing. Then add the assertion this class of bug needs: a test that reads the built stylesheet and fails if any class used in src/ has no corresponding rule, which catches the whole namespace family rather than this one instance.

review.title: The comment justifying the unlayered .skip-link:focus rule states a cascade fact that is false, and the rule is unnecessary for the reason it gives. `focus:mb-space-2` does not lose to `not-sr-only`'s `margin: 0`; it wins, because Tailwind emits margin-bottom after margin within the utilities layer. review.detail:
The comment justifying the unlayered .skip-link:focus rule states a cascade fact that is false, and the rule is unnecessary for the reason it gives. `focus:mb-space-2` does not lose to `not-sr-only`'s `margin: 0`; it wins, because Tailwind emits margin-bottom after margin within the utilities layer. A future reader who checks will find the comment wrong and may delete a rule that is currently doing the work.

`src/app/globals.css:81`

Evidence: The comment claims 'both live in @layer utilities, and utilities sort by property so margin is emitted first'. In the built stylesheet both rules are indeed inside @layer utilities (which spans bytes 6192..13596), but `.focus\:not-sr-only:focus` sits at byte 12441 and `.focus\:mb-space-2:focus` at byte 12851 — the margin-bottom rule is emitted 410 bytes LATER, so at equal specificity it is the winner, not the loser. Sorting by property puts margin (shorthand) before margin-bottom (longhand), which is exactly what makes the later longhand override. Confirmed in Chromium against the running build at localhost:3111: with the .skip-link class removed from the skip link and focus:mb-space-2 appended in its place, the focused link still computes margin-bottom 8px and the gap to the top-bar brand link is still 16px, identical to production. The same holds in an isolated harness stripped of the unlayered rule: `sr-only focus:not-sr-only ... focus:mb-space-2` with no .skip-link class still measures margin-bottom 8px. So the rule is load-bearing for the class as written (strip the rule and the shipped skip link drops to margin-bottom 0px and dy=0 — I confirmed that too), but the stated reason for needing it does not hold.

Fix: Either delete the unlayered rule and put `focus:mb-space-2` in the skip link's className, which measures identically and keeps the spacing in the design system where every other gap lives, or keep the rule and rewrite the comment to say what is actually true — that an unlayered rule outranks every layered one regardless of order, without asserting that the utility loses. The first is smaller and is what I would do.

triage.diagnosis: The root-cause agent produced no output at all, and the red step is three steps downstream of that. It ran 110 turns for 27 minutes and $5.59 and wrote neither work-order.json nor stop.json — its only two Write calls went to /tmp/probe/t14.mjs and /tmp/probe/sweep.mjs, scratch files outside the repository that the upload path (work-order.json, stop.json, root-cause-transcript.json) never picks up, which is why the root-cause-output artifact is 421 bytes and holds only the transcript. The agent still reported success: the result line reads subtype success, is_error false, num_turns 110, and the diagnose job exited green. The failure surfaced in publish at step 'Number the revision', where bump-version.mjs:22 does readFileSync on a work-order.json that was never written and dies with a bare ENOENT — a missing-input crash that names a file nobody was supposed to produce, so the log points at version bookkeeping rather than at the agent that returned nothing. The framework cannot currently tell those two cases apart: sdlc-root-cause.yml guards the stop branch with hashFiles('stop.json') != '' but guards bump-version, validate, check-forbidden and post-work-order only on steps.stop.outputs.stopped != 'true', which is equally true when the agent wrote nothing, and there is no hashFiles('work-order.json') guard anywhere in the file. That also defeats the workflow's own stated intent at the download step — continue-on-error: true with the comment 'validation says so by name' — because bump-version runs before validation and kills the job first, so the validation that was meant to name the failure never runs. This is not transient and not a plan defect: nothing timed out, no rate or quota limit was hit, the provider returned success, and prior_signatures is empty with occurrences 1, so this exact signature is new — but the pattern of an agent spending 27 minutes and returning nothing is not something a retry fixes by itself, and I cannot explain why the agent abandoned the task after 110 turns from this log: it records 104 Bash calls and two /tmp probes but not the reason it stopped short. Escalating for a person rather than rerunning on a guess. The expensive work did NOT survive and resume would be a lie — the probe scripts went to /tmp on a runner that no longer exists.
